paragraph: [UNESCO's readiness assessment of Angola, published in July 2026](<https://www.unesco.org/ethics-ai/en/angola>), lists formal approval of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy as a next step, so a draft exists and the government has not approved it. [In November 2026 the minister told an ITU conference that the strategy was still being prepared](<https://pti.ao/angola-apresenta-a-uit-projectos-de-fibra-optica-satelite-e-cloud/>), with no date set. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body or public money for the strategy. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

Burundi's national AI strategy for 2025 to 2030 was [validated in Bujumbura in April 2026 with UNDP support](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/intelligence-artificielle-a-seoul-le-burundi-presente-ses-ambitions>). [The validation session opened on 21 April 2026](<https://abpinfo.bi/2026/04/22/validation-de-la-strategie-nationale-de-lia/>), and [the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy designed the strategy](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burundi-rolls-out-six-pillar-ai-strategy-to-accelerate-digital-economy>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the government has approved or launched it, or names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[The Council of Ministers adopted Benin's national strategy for AI and big data, covering 2023 to 2027, on 18 January 2023](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-benin>). [It has 123 actions and a projected budget of 4.68 billion CFA francs over five years](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-benin>). [In July 2026 a ministry official said a university's AI strategy was in line with the national one](<https://lanation.bj/numerique/intelligence-artificielle-luac-adopte-une-strategie-un-cadre-ethique-et-une-charte-dusage>). In the last twelve months the strategy was cited and not changed. No source found names a body set up to carry it out, or public money allocated to it. Operating would need the government to name a body to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit.

[The Ministry of Digital Transition held a validation workshop on Burkina Faso's national AI roadmap for 2026 to 2030 on 17 June 2026](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/17/burkina-faso-validates-national-ai-roadmap-2026-2030-to-accelerate-digital-transformation/>). On 23 October 2026 the ministry [presented the roadmap, with a budget of FCFA 30 billion, as validated and awaiting publication](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2710-142784-burkina-faso-les-ambitions-ia-en-langues-locales-face-au-defi-des-donnees>). The ministry [had begun drafting an AI action plan at a workshop in 2025](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202509/national-ai-strategy-to-guide-burkina-fasos-digital-transformation>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the roadmap is adopted, or names a body set up for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[On 13 August 2025 the Assistant Minister of Communications and Innovation said the government was finalising Botswana's National Artificial Intelligence Policy](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/88106>). [In July 2026 a Parliament of Botswana research brief said the government was still working toward a final draft](<https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7263340>). [In November 2026 the president of the Botswana Information Technology Society said the policy had been submitted to Parliament](<https://itweb.africa/article/southern-africas-ai-ambitions-face-reality-check/KWEBbvyLd4mqmRjO>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the policy is adopted, or names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[On 21 November 2024 the minister of posts, telecommunications and digital economy said the Central African Republic was in the full drafting phase of its national AI strategy for 2024 to 2028](<https://cio-mag.com/atda-2024-lia-et-le-developpement-durable-au-menu-de-la-session-officielle/>). No source found dated since then says whether the draft has been finished, approved or launched. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body or public money for the strategy. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[On 13 March 2025 the digital transition minister handed Cote d'Ivoire's AI strategy to the Prime Minister, to go to the government for adoption](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/cote-divoire-les-axes-de-la-strategie-nationale-de-l-ia-et-de-la-strategie-nationale-de-la-gouvernance-des-donnees/>). In the last twelve months, [on 11 September 2026 the minister said the government would speed up its implementation](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2644463/economie/impact-ia-2026-la-cote-divoire-passe-de-la-reflexion-a-laction-avec-77-cas-dusage-prioritaires>). [In November 2026 AIP reported a firm helping the ministry draft a 2026-2030 AI strategy](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-les-senateurs-formes-aux-enjeux-et-aux-applications-de-lintelligence-artificielle-a-yamoussoukro/>). No source found says the government adopted the strategy, or names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications unveiled Cameroon's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy at national consultations on 7 and 8 July 2025](<https://leconomie.info/strategie-nationale-de-lintelligence-artificielle-un-cadre-clair-pour-le-futur-numerique-du-cameroun/>). In May 2026 the PATNUC coordinator said [the AI strategic development plan still awaited validation by the competent institutions](<https://cameroon-tribune.cm/article.html/76479/en.html/bold-initiatives-are-being-undertaken-at-accelerating-digital-transformation>). In the last twelve months the position has been unveiled and awaiting validation. [A policy brief of September 2026 found the AI authority and the presidential council were not in place](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202611/africas-ai-ambitions-depend-on-stronger-digital-public-infrastructure-expert-says>). No source found says the strategy has been validated. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[Public bodies, partners and experts validated the national AI strategy of the Democratic Republic of the Congo at a ceremony in Kinshasa on 4 August 2026](<https://www.unesco.org/fr/articles/la-rdc-se-dote-dune-strategie-nationale-pour-une-intelligence-artificielle-ethique-et-inclusive>). [The minister said it would go to the Council of Ministers within days for adoption](<https://actu7.cd/2026/08/04/rdc-augustin-kibassa-lance-la-politique-sectorielle-de-leconomie-numerique-et-la-strategie-nationale-de-lia-pour-batir-un-congo-souverain-connecte-innovant-et-inclusif/>). In the last twelve months it went from drafting, with [a commission set up on 8 October 2025](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-democratic-republic-of-congo>), to validation. No source found says the council has adopted it, or names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[The government of the Republic of the Congo, with UNDP support, held a national workshop in Brazzaville on 6 and 7 May 2026 that launched the drafting of a national AI strategy](<https://www.aci.cg/congo-technologie-necessite-dintegrer-un-comite-national-dethique-dans-la-future-strategie-nationale-de-lia/>). The final document was still to be written. No source found dated since then says how far the drafting has gone. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body or public money for the strategy. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[Al-watwan reports that the UNESCO readiness assessment presented in September 2026 finds Comoros has no national AI strategy](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/intelligence-artificielle-i-le-diagnostic-ram-2.0-r%C3%A9v%C3%A8le-les-d%C3%A9fis-des-comores.html>). It says drafting one is the first step still to be taken. [In February 2025 an official of the digital agency Anaden told Al-watwan there was no national AI policy](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/intelligence-artificielle-i-les-comores-ne-disposent-toujours-pas-d%E2%80%99une-politique-en-mati%C3%A8re-d%E2%80%99ia.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether any drafting has begun, or names a body or funding. Preparing would need a national AI strategy, policy or roadmap being written or out for consultation, or a task force appointed to write it.

[The government of Cape Verde launched the development of a national AI strategy at a kick-off meeting reported held on 28 April 2026](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/05/04/cape-verde-launches-national-data-and-ai-strategies-to-modernize-public-administration/>). Government officials, external consultants and European Union representatives attended. The strategy was still to be written. No source found dated since then says how far the drafting has gone. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[In September 2026 the government presented Djibouti's first national AI strategy and launched it](<https://lobservateur.info/article/119465/covid-19/intelligence-artificielle-djibouti-lance-sa-premiere-strategie-nationale>). It runs from 2026 to 2030, with six priority axes. [In January 2026 a workshop on the draft was held ahead of its official adoption](<https://www.unescwa.org/news/developing-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy-djibouti>). [One report of the September 2026 forum](<https://www.lanation.dj/premier-forum-national-sur-lintelligence-artificielle-djibouti-devoile-sa-strategie-nationale-2026-2030/>) has the strategy presented there without saying it was adopted. In the last twelve months the strategy went from a draft to a launch. No source found names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[On 25 May 2026 a government meeting chaired by the Prime Minister examined Algeria's draft national AI strategy](<https://www.aps.dz/fr/algerie/actualite-nationale/mpl9oi57-la-strategie-nationale-d-intelligence-artificielle-a-l-ordre-du-jour>). [El Moudjahid reports that action plans are to follow its adoption by the Council of Ministers](<https://www.elmoudjahid.dz/fr/actualite/reunion-du-gouvernement-la-strategie-nationale-d-intelligence-artificielle-a-l-ordre-du-jour-252722>). [Algerie Eco reports that a first version was announced in December 2024](<https://algerie-eco.com/2024/12/08/lalgerie-adopte-une-strategie-nationale-de-lia/>). [On 3 November 2026 the higher education minister chaired the sixth meeting on carrying it out](<https://www.mesrs.dz/fr/2026/11/le-ministre-de-lenseignement-superieur-et-de-la-recherche-scientifique-preside-la-sixieme-reunion-multisectorielle-consacree-au-suivi-de-la-mise-en-oeuvre-de-la-strategie-nationale-de-l/>). In the last twelve months it went from a first version announced in December 2024 to a draft examined in May 2026. No source found says the Council of Ministers has adopted the strategy. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[The ICT minister said the second edition of Egypt's National AI Strategy, for 2025 to 2030, was launched in January 2025](<https://mcit.gov.eg/en/Media_Center/Press_Room/Press_Releases/68238>). [The National Council for AI, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies follows up the strategy](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/25/egypt-ai-council-national-ai-strategy-quantum-computing/>). [In March 2026 the council asked government bodies to report every quarter against the implementation plan](<https://mcit.gov.eg/en/Media_Center/Latest_News/News/99046>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from the last three years names public money allocated to the strategy. Mature would need a dated source naming public money allocated to the strategy, or an action in it started with its funding named.

No stage is set. [A legal-status page last reviewed on 8 June 2026 says Eritrea has no national AI strategy and no published national AI policy](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-eritrea>). It does not say whether one is being written. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the country has no national AI strategy and that none is being written.

[The Council of Ministers approved Ethiopia's National Artificial Intelligence Policy on 27 June 2024, with immediate effect](<https://ethiopianmonitor.com/2024/06/28/council-approves-ethiopias-first-artificial-intelligence-policy/>). [The policy names the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute as the national coordinating body for implementation](<https://cipesa.org/2026/07/rethinking-africas-approach-to-the-politics-of-ai-governance-and-regulation/>). [In February 2026 the institute's director general said the country had recently published the policy](<https://www.undp.org/ethiopia/press-releases/ethiopia-launches-ai-unipod>). In the last twelve months the policy was cited and not changed. No source found from the last three years names public money allocated to the strategy. Mature would need a dated source naming public money allocated to the strategy, or an action in it started with its funding named.

[Preparatory workshops for Gabon's national AI strategy closed in Libreville on 30 September 2026, with 22 challenges and 36 recommendations from six groups supported by UNDP](<https://www.gabonreview.com/22-defis-36-recommandations-la-feuille-de-route-de-lia-gabonaise-prend-forme/>). [UNDP said the document presented was a first diagnostic, not a finished strategy](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-ia-fin-des-travaux-sur-la-future-strategie-nationale/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a strategy is adopted, or names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[President Mahama launched Ghana's National AI Strategy for 2025 to 2035 in Accra on 24 April 2026](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/04/ghana-to-invest-250m-in-ai-centre-launch-national-strategy-2/>). [Cabinet had approved it in February 2026](<https://www.citinewsroom.com/2026/02/ghanas-national-ai-strategy-secures-cabinet-approval-sam-george/>). [In July 2026 the government said it was writing a ten-year implementation plan with yearly milestones](<https://thechronicle.com.gh/government-rolls-out-10-year-ai-implementation-roadmap-to-drive-jobs-economic-growth/>). In the last twelve months the strategy was cited and not changed. No source found names a body set up or named to carry it out. Operating would need the government to name a body to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit.

[On 19 and 20 December 2025 the ministry of posts, telecommunications and the digital economy validated a national AI roadmap for 2026 to 2035 at a workshop with UNDP](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/2212-51603-guinea-validates-10-year-national-ai-roadmap>). [The ministry's report on 2025 lists the roadmap among the year's work](<https://www.africaguinee.com/app/uploads/2026/01/Realisations_MPTEN_2025_compressed.pdf>). [In September 2026 the higher-education ministry named finalising the national strategy document as a next step](<https://www.csig.edu.gn/actualites/la-cite-des-sciences-et-de-linnovation-au-cur-du-digital-cooperation-day-la-guinee-trace-sa-voie-vers-lia-souveraine/>). No source found says the government adopted the strategy, or names a body or public money for it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[In its national statement to a United Nations commission meeting in Geneva in April 2026, The Gambia said it was developing a National AI Policy and Strategy, led by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy](<https://unctad.org/system/files/non-official-document/ecn162026_s08_ai_gambia_en.pdf>). No source found dated since then says how far the drafting has gone. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

No stage is set. [Digital Watch says Guinea-Bissau has no confirmed standalone AI strategy](<https://dig.watch/countries/guinea-bissau>). It does not say whether one is being written. No source found says whether any drafting has begun. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the country has no national AI strategy and that none is being written.

[The ICT Cabinet Secretary launched Kenya's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for 2025 to 2030 in Nairobi on 27 March 2025](<https://citizen.digital/article/kenya-launches-national-ai-strategy-with-ksh152b-implementation-budget-n359983>). [On 30 June 2026 the Cabinet set up a Standing Cabinet Committee on Artificial Intelligence to steer the strategy](<https://cipit.strathmore.edu/the-standing-cabinet-committee-on-artificial-intelligence-implications-for-kenyas-evolving-ai-ecosystem/>). [A review of the 2026/27 national budget found no dedicated allocation for the strategy](<https://cipesa.org/2026/07/rethinking-africas-approach-to-the-politics-of-ai-governance-and-regulation/>). In the last twelve months the committee was added to the strategy launched in March 2025. Mature would need a dated source naming public money allocated to the strategy, or an action in it started with its funding named.

[The Prime Minister of the Government of National Unity launched Libya's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for 2026 to 2030 on 1 June 2026](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=358532&lang=en>). [A meeting on 26 April 2026 dealt with moving the strategy from preparation to implementation](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/05/03/the-general-authority-for-information-hosts-an-extensive-meeting-to-launch-the-executive-initiatives-of-the-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy/>). In the last twelve months it went from preparation in April 2026 to launch in June 2026. No source found names a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit set up to carry it out. Operating would need the government to name a body to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit.

The ICT minister [told the World Governments Summit in February 2026](<https://www.lena.gov.ls/lesotho-represented-at-the-2026-world-governments-summit-in-dudai/>) that the government approved Lesotho's National Artificial Intelligence Policy in the second half of 2025. [The policy and its implementation plan were published on 17 August 2026](<https://cadeproject.org/updates/lesotho-moves-from-ai-policy-to-national-strategy-and-digital-infrastructure-planning/>). The ICT ministry and the United Nations [began work on a national AI strategy at a five-day workshop in Maseru](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/18/lesotho-begins-work-on-national-ai-strategy-and-data-centre-blueprint/>) from 17 August 2026. In the last twelve months the policy went from approved in 2025 to published. No source found names a body set up to carry it out. Operating would need the government to name a body to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit.

[On 10 November 2026 the minister for digital transition told parliament he was launching Morocco AI 2030](<https://en.hespress.com/148882-morocco-develops-national-ai-roadmap-as-government-seeks-to-regulate-technology-use.html>), a national AI roadmap with three pillars and 10 programmes. [In January 2026 the digital minister told parliament that a programme called AI Made in Morocco was being drawn up](<https://fr.alyaoum24.com/numerique-et-innovation/53166.html>). [A decree of 26 October 2026 charged minister Ahmed Rahhou with drawing up the government's AI policy](<https://medias24.com/2026/10/28/ahmed-rahhou-charge-delaborer-la-politique-publique-en-matiere-dia-1785031/>). No source found says the government has adopted the roadmap, or names a body or public money for it. In the last twelve months the programme of January 2026 became the roadmap of November 2026. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

No stage is set. [An expert said in October 2026 that, to his knowledge, Mali had no published national AI strategy](<https://amap.ml/2026/10/23/intelligence-artificielle-et-souverainete-numerique-le-mali-face-aux-defis-de-la-gouvernance-et-de-la-desinformation/>). No source found says whether one is being written. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the country has no national AI strategy and that none is being written.

[A first draft of Mozambique's National AI Strategy for 2026 to 2031 is dated April 2026](<https://www.africaainews.com/api/v1/file/4d6b91fa-97e7-4576-9c5f-57e3aea89fbe.pdf>), and [the first version was out for public consultation from 4 May to 4 June 2026](<https://intic.gov.mz/consulta-publica-da-proposta-da-estrategia-nacional-de-inteligencia-artificial/>). [A decree of 17 April 2026 created a National AI Commission under the Council of Ministers](<https://intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/BR_72_I_SERIE_2026_CNIA.pdf>). [In October 2026 the ICT institute was still inviting comments on the proposal](<https://mznews.co.mz/mocambique-prepara-formadores-para-uso-da-inteligencia-artificial-nas-eleicoes/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the strategy is adopted, or names public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[In July 2024 the digital ministry issued a final edition of Mauritania's National AI Strategy for 2025 to 2029, with thirteen axes](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/strategie-AR-Final-26-07-2024-.pdf>). [A country commercial guide of February 2026 says the ministry has published the strategy](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/mauritania-digital-economy>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. [Ecofin Agency reported in October 2026 that it covers healthcare, education, agriculture and transportation](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0910-59612-mauritanias-digital-economy-plans-face-persistent-telecom-network-quality-problems>). No source found says the Council of Ministers approved it, or names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[Cabinet agreed on 13 February 2026 to adopt Mauritius's National AI Strategy for 2025 to 2029 as the national guiding framework for AI](<https://pmo.govmu.org/CabinetDecision/2026/Highlights%20of%20Cabinet%20Meeting%20%20Friday%20%2013%20February%202026.pdf>). [It was launched in April 2026 together with a set of guidelines](<https://cajnewsafrica.com/2026/08/21/mauritius-commissions-pioneering-ai-innovation-lab/>), and [replaced the 2018 strategy after a review](<https://acetforafrica.org/research-and-analysis/insights-ideas/who-funds-ai-policy-development-in-africa/>). [The minister said an AI Unit was set up in December 2025 to complement the strategy](<https://cajnewsafrica.com/2026/08/21/mauritius-commissions-pioneering-ai-innovation-lab/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from the last three years names public money allocated to the strategy. Mature would need a dated source naming public money allocated to the strategy, or an action in it started with its funding named.

[The Ministry of ICT's Department of E-Government, with UNDP, began validating Malawi's draft National AI Strategy at a two-day workshop in Lilongwe in February 2026](<https://cajnewsafrica.com/2026/02/20/malawi-validates-ai-strategy-digital-transformation-policy/>). [On 6 August 2026 the ICT minister said the government was finalising the strategy, to be supported by an AI bill](<https://itweb.africa/article/malawi-drafts-ai-bill-to-govern-public-sector-tech/PmxVE7KEOnpqQY85>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the strategy has been approved, or names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[In August 2026 the ICT minister said consultations on Namibia's national AI strategy framework had begun, led by the national research commission](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/05/namibia-and-deloitte-discuss-ai-strategy-and-digital-infrastructure-development/>). [In September 2026 the commission's chief executive said the strategy, developed with 215 local experts and stakeholders, had reached national validation, before it goes to the minister and then Cabinet](<https://www.namibian.com.na/national-ai-institute-launched/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the strategy is adopted, or names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[The communications minister announced the launch of Nigeria's national AI strategy in Lagos in April 2025](<https://www.channelstv.com/2025/04/16/nigeria-launches-national-ai-strategy-to-drive-ai-development-boost-productivity/>). [In September 2025 a professor said the strategy was yet to be approved by the Federal Executive Council](<https://thefact.ng/experts-call-for-national-policy-on-ai-development-deployment-in-nigeria/>). In the last twelve months the strategy stayed awaiting approval. [In March 2026 the minister said it would go to the National Assembly for approval](<https://punchng.com/govt-finalises-ai-policy-seeks-legislative-backing/>). No source found says the Council or the Assembly has approved it. None names a body or public money for it. Establishing would need a national AI strategy adopted and still running, approved by cabinet or formally validated by the government.

[The Prime Minister said in September 2026 that the government has adopted Rwanda's National AI Policy](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/39113/news/rwanda/energy-compute-capacity-the-biggest-constraints-to-rwandas-ai-ambitions-pm>). [The policy gives the Responsible AI Office under the Ministry of ICT and Innovation the job of implementing it](<https://cipesa.org/2026/07/rethinking-africas-approach-to-the-politics-of-ai-governance-and-regulation/>). In the last twelve months, [on 8 June 2026 Cabinet approved the creation of a National Artificial Intelligence Agency](<https://www.ktpress.rw/2026/06/rwandas-ai-ambition-takes-shape-as-cabinet-approves-new-agency/>), following the 2023 policy. No source found from the last three years names public money allocated to the strategy.
